public_rationale: The proposed mechanism is plausible, and a [randomized study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35703413/) shows that useful assistance can leave interpretation with radiologists. The [ESR survey](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35727355/) also shows that assistance often brought no reported workload reduction. Neither source directly tests the asserted causal comparison.
limitations: Successful assistance is not itself a measurement of development difficulty.
Lack of workload reduction does not prove assistance is as difficult as replacement.
The evidence covers a narrow set of medical applications.

our_interpretation: The plain reading compares useful assistance with autonomous performance of the same occupation's full duties.
Easier means materially lower capability and engineering requirements at a comparable standard of useful, reliable service.
The proposed mechanism is that people retain duties the machine cannot perform. Mere adoption of assistance does not establish this mechanism or its size.
The claim concerns the technical situation at publication, rather than an unconditional law about every occupation.
criteria.support_condition: Comparisons or task analyses show that retaining difficult duties with people materially reduces the capabilities and engineering effort needed for useful assistance relative to full replacement.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence shows that effective assistance generally requires essentially the same capabilities and effort as full replacement, or that human-machine coordination removes the claimed advantage.
